title: Lansing Insulation Rebates 2026: BWL $100 per Measure and Consumers Up to $475
desc: Lansing insulation rebates in 2026: BWL pays $100 per measure for electric homes, Consumers Energy pays $50 to $200 per area for gas homes. Rules, dates and free help.
lead: Which insulation rebate you get in Lansing depends on how you heat. If you heat with electricity or have central air, the Board of Water & Light pays $100 per measure. If you heat with gas from Consumers Energy, its chart pays $50 to $200 per area. We read both on October 6, 2026.
cards_heading: What insulation rebates pay in Lansing
cards_intro: BWL's amounts are from its 2026 rebate form. Consumers' amounts are from its windows and insulation chart. Both end on December 31.

cards.title: BWL attic insulation
cards.note: Must reach R-49 or more, starting from R-11 or less, and cover at least 500 square feet.

cards.title: BWL wall and basement wall insulation
cards.note: Walls need R-7 or more over 500 square feet. Basement walls need R-20 or more over 500 square feet.

cards.title: BWL air sealing
cards.note: Needs blower door tests before and after, with at least 30% less leakage.

cards.title: Consumers attic insulation
cards.note: For gas and combination customers, by R-value. Electric-only customers get $50 to $70.

cards.title: Consumers walls and rim joist
cards.note: Above-grade walls $125, basement walls $50, rim joist $50 for gas and combination customers.

cards.title: State weatherization
cards.note: For households at or below 200% of the federal poverty level.

cards.title: Federal 25C and 25D tax credits
cards.note: The federal home energy credits ended for work finished after December 31, 2025. A quote that counts on them is out of date.

sections: BWL says insulation rebates are for its residential electric customers who have central air conditioning or electric heat, including heat pumps and electric resistance heating. Consumers' chart is for its customers with the matching service, and gas customers get the larger amounts. Many Lansing homes have BWL electric and Consumers gas, so one project can fit both. Do not assume you can claim both on one measure. Ask each company.

The Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) says 79.5% of Lansing homes were built before 1980 and 24.5% before 1940. Utility gas heats 74.6% of homes. In those homes the attic is the first place to look, then the rim joist.

Insulation works best after the leaks are sealed. A blower door test before and after shows how much air you stopped. BWL pays $50 when leakage drops by 30%, and the same test records can support other applications. Ask your contractor to seal the attic floor before adding material, since warm air that leaks into the attic can waste the new insulation.

46.2% of Lansing households rent, and 7.5% of homes are in buildings of two to four units. Consumers covers buildings with fewer than three units, and BWL's form is for the residential electric account holder. A tenant who pays the bills still needs the landlord's written approval to change the building.

BWL needs a detailed invoice that names the type of insulation, the R-value installed and the square feet covered. Consumers needs a participating contractor and wants the paperwork filed by December 31. Read each form before you sign, because a missing R-value on an invoice can sink an application.

If your household income is at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, Michigan's weatherization program installs insulation and air sealing at no cost through local agencies. Michigan's MiHER program, which can pay more, is paused for new income-qualified applications in the Lansing district.
claim_heading: How to claim insulation rebates in Lansing
claim_steps: Look at your bills to see who supplies electricity and who supplies gas.
Get two quotes that list the type of insulation, R-value and square feet.
Ask each rebate program whether you can claim both on a single job.
For BWL, apply by email, fax or mail with your invoice by December 31, 2026.
For Consumers, make sure the contractor files the application on time.
faq: How much does BWL pay for insulation?
$100 for attic, wall or basement wall work that meets its R-value and area rules, plus $50 for cutting air leakage by 30%.
How much does Consumers pay for attic insulation?
$125 to $200 for gas and combination customers, depending on R-value.
The rebate goes to the account holder, so a renter needs the landlord's approval and help.
BWL does not accept applications after December 31, 2026. Consumers' chart lists December 31.
Does the federal insulation credit apply?
No. It ended for work finished after December 31, 2025.
